Held a very productive meeting of the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation. Thank First DPM Denis Manturov for co-chairing this key mechanism. 

Our discussions focused on our wide - ranging cooperation in trade, investments, energy, fertilizers, nuclear, connectivity, technology, space and mobility domains. 

As our economic partnership enters the next phase, underscored the importance of :

➡️ Focusing on implementation and outcomes to prioritise sector - specific deliverables and actively engage in problem - solving. 

➡️ Further strengthening our engagement with businesses by aligning institutional mechanisms with industry priorities, identifying practical bottlenecks and improving policy responsiveness. 

➡️ Constantly updating our view of opportunities and exploring new possibilities. To realise our complementarities and address the needs of de-risking and diversifying. 

Confident that our meeting today will go a long way in deepening our practical cooperation across a range of domains.

✅ The global order is uncertain and volatile where interdependence and common interests co-exist with competitiveness and rivalries.

✅ India stands for finding a political solution to the Myanmar issue; even as we continue to support the ASEAN efforts.
 
✅ Demand serious collective action against cyber scam centres, which have victimised Indian nationals in significant numbers.

✅ India has made notable relief and rehabilitation contributions and is a top emerging donor of UNRWA. We believe that a two-state solution can lead to a lasting and durable peace.

Delighted to meet my fellow Foreign Ministers from #EuropeanUnion today in Brussels. Thank EU HRVP @kajakallas for inviting me to this Foreign Affairs Council Meeting.

A new chapter in India-EU ties has opened up in 2026. The Foreign Ministers coordinate translating the various agreements into outcomes. Our conversation today therefore covered trade, investment, technology, mobility and defence in particular.

The stronger convergence between India and EU in a multipolar world is also expressed in closer consultations. Discussed the West Asia conflict, the Ukraine situation and the Indo-Pacific in today’s gathering.

Concluded a productive visit to Brussels, meeting with the #EuropeanUnion Foreign Affairs Council, calling on Presidents of the European Council António Costa and European Commission @ursulavonderleyen, and holding talks with EU HRVP @kajakallas. Also met EU counterparts and held separate bilateral discussions with many.

Ten key messages in these conversations were:

✅ The finalization of the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) represents a turning point in 🇮🇳 🇪🇺 ties. Will not only unlock its enormous economic potential but express the strategic nature of our engagement. 

✅ To realize the gains of FTA on the ground, the two sides should proactively assist each other in practical activities, including trade and investment promotion.

✅ The Trade and Technology Council (TTC) can be upgraded and repurposed to facilitate collaboration in critical and cutting-edge technologies. 

✅ De-risking supply chains and enhancing resilience are shared objectives. The FTA will encourage deeper business linkages to that end.

✅ Mobility of skills and talent flows are very important. The establishment of the Legal Gateway Office in India is noteworthy. We have a common interest in promoting Global Capability Centers (GCCs) in India.

✅ The Security and Defence Partnership will be taken forward. Will endeavour to conclude the Security of Information Agreement early. 

✅ Connectivity is also prominent in our agenda. Will work together to give practical shape to IMEC and other such initiatives. 

✅ As multilateralism comes under stress, India and the EU will strive to strengthen its institutions and practices.

✅ Our Strategic Partnership will be carried out through close and regular consultations at the leadership level. Domain specific mechanisms will support those efforts. 

✅ In a multipolar and uncertain world, the India-EU partnership will act as a factor of stability and resilience.

Attended the conference on ‘50 Years of the Biological Weapons Convention: Strengthening Bio-security for the Global South’, in New Delhi today.

Spoke to experts and representatives from 80+ countries about modernising the Convention, the critical role of India and the Global South.

Emphasized the need for:

➡️ Ensuring that BWC remains the guardrail between innovation and misuse in the life sciences in an uncertain international security environment.

➡️ Realizing that BWC lacks basic institutional structures like absence of compliance system, permanent technical body or tracking mechanism for new scientific developments. 

➡️ Working to modernize the Convention, stronger compliance measures, keeping pace with S&T and strengthening global capacity.

➡️ Securing international cooperation as central to any solution, considering biological threat moves fast, defies borders and overwhelms systems.

➡️ Ensuring that Global South shapes the next 50 years of BWC as it has most to gain from stronger biosecurity and also the most to contribute.

Also highlighted 🇮🇳’s:

➡️ Commitment to full and effective BWC implementation.

➡️ Record of ensuring non-proliferation of sensitive and dual-use goods & technologies.

➡️ Vaccine Maitri initiative during the COVID-19 pandemic.

➡️ Proposal of a National Implementation Framework that covers identification of high-risk agents, oversight of dual-use research, domestic reporting, incident management, and continuous training. 

As we strive to modernize the BWC, the Global South must take ownership—preparing wisely for future challenges.

A global lifeline, the Indian Ocean region comes together to meet its development, connectivity, maritime and security aspirations. 

Highlighted how India is contributing to these shared endeavours:

1️⃣ As a stable partner and friend in times of COVID, food & fuel shortages or even economic crisis.

2️⃣ As a promoter of greater land and sea connectivity -  be it IMEC, IMTT or INSTC.

3️⃣ In becoming a first responder to conflicts and disasters in the region, both natural and man made.

4️⃣ By promoting interoperability and synergies with partners to face maritime contingencies and piracy. 

5️⃣ Ensuring maritime safety and security by establishing coastal surveillance radars and partnering on White Shipping agreements.

6️⃣ In responding to extreme situations through deployment of naval forces.

7️⃣ Though capacity - building of other Indian Ocean Navies and coast guards.

8️⃣ By ensuring trusted and secure communication in a digital era. 

9️⃣ In closing gaps and building bridges between resident and non resident powers with the Global South. And discouraging alien agendas.

🔟 Supporting institution building in the region, be it IORA, BIMSTEC, IONS, CSC, IPOI or the Indian Ocean Conference itself.
